translation: Chaihu (Bupleurum), Chuanxiong (Ligusticum), Chuan Dahuang (rhubarb), Chishaoyao (red peony), Danggui (Angelica), Zhizi (Gardenia), Wulingzhi (flying squirrel droppings), Mutong (Akebia), Zhishi (immature bitter orange, stir-fried), Honghua (safflower), Chiniuxi (red Achyranthes), Zelanye (Lycopus leaf), Sumu (sappan wood), Shengdihuang (raw Rehmannia), Huangqin (Scutellaria), Taoren (peach kernel). Decoct in water, add old wine and boy's urine, and take together. <ins>Jiajian Zijin Dan</ins> (Modified Purple-Gold Pill, 加減紫金丹): Baifuling (Poria), Cangzhu (Atractylodes lancea, soaked in rice water, stir-fried, two liang each), Danggui (Angelica), Shudihuang (cooked Rehmannia), Baishaoyao (white peony, stir-fried), Chenpi (tangerine peel, four liang each), Roucongrong (Cistanche, washed in wine and scales removed, one liang), Dingxiang (clove, one qian), Honghua (safflower, five qian), Guaer Xuejie (dragon's blood, three qian), Ruxiang (frankincense, oil removed, three qian), Moyao (myrrh, oil removed, three qian). Grind all together into a fine powder, refine honey into pills the size of a pellet (彈子), and take with yellow wine.
